name: How does finish carpentry differ when remodeling older Salt Lake City homes compared to newer builds?

mainEntity.name: How does finish carpentry differ when remodeling older Salt Lake City homes compared to newer builds?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older Salt Lake City neighborhoods such as Sugar House, The Avenues, and Central City often feature historic homes with original wide baseboards, tall picture rails, and lath-and-plaster walls that are rarely plumb or level. Working in these homes requires custom scribing, back-cutting, and sometimes milling custom profiles to match historic details. In contrast, newer construction or open-concept suburban remodels in areas like South Jordan or Riverton typically feature standard drywall and modern, simplified profiles that install more predictably.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older Salt Lake homes often have uneven plaster walls requiring custom scribing and historic profile matching, while newer builds use standard drywall and streamlined trim profiles.
